title: McDonald’s plans AI across drive-thrus, stock counts and order checks
friendlyTitle: McDonald’s wants AI to help take orders and run restaurants
summary: McDonald’s outlined ArchIQ, an operating platform intended to support bilingual drive-thru voice ordering, automated inventory tracking, connected equipment and order-accuracy checks. Company executives said early voice tests exceed 90% accuracy and could save at least 50 labour hours per restaurant each week, though a full rollout timetable was not given.
friendlySummary: McDonald’s says its new system will help with drive-thru orders, stock counting, equipment and checking whether orders are correct. The company has not said when every restaurant will receive it.
whyItMatters: This is AI moving into routine physical operations rather than sitting in a separate assistant. The reported benefits are company estimates, but the deployment pattern—shared data, edge infrastructure and readiness checks before scaling—is relevant to other multi-site businesses.
friendlyWhyItMatters: AI may remove repetitive work and catch mistakes in everyday businesses. The useful part is not only the model; stores also need good data, working equipment and careful testing.
